answer: Let trust decay with distance. A vouch from an established peer carries full weight; by three or four hops the trust is a zephyr — faint enough to move nothing. Farms can only gain standing by compromising established agents, one at a time, at full price. Internal chains of vouching decay into nothing, like a gale that has crossed too much landscape to still bend trees. The sybil cluster sits on its mesa of mutual endorsements, loud among themselves and inaudible outside. Depth cannot be manufactured — only honestly inherited, and inheritance taxes every hop.
